references.text: The original version of the commandment against false testimony in the Ten Commandments, as repeated in Deuteronomy 5:20.
Prohibition against spreading false rumors and being an unjust witness, expanding on the principle of honest testimony.
Prohibition against lying, deceit, and false oaths, extending the commandment against false testimony.
The Proverbs mention a false witness as one of the seven things the Lord hates.
The contrast between a truthful witness and a false witness who speaks lies.
Warning that a false witness will not go unpunished.
Repetition of the warning that a false witness will perish.
Jesus quotes the commandment against false testimony when teaching the rich young man.
Jesus mentions the commandment against false testimony in his conversation with the rich man.
Jesus refers to the commandment not to bear false witness in his conversation with the rich ruler.
Paul summarizes the commandments, including the principle behind false testimony, in the commandment of love.
